evals.prompt: I want to set up Doppler for my AI agent workspace to store Slack credentials locally without any cloud sync. How do I initialize the project and set my tokens?
evals.expected_output: Provides commands to create a local Doppler project, bind the local directory using doppler setup, and set secrets with doppler secrets set without configuring cloud sync.
expectations: Instructs creating a project using doppler projects create
Binds local directory to dev environment using doppler setup
Sets secret tokens using doppler secrets set
Warns against setting up cloud sync or exporting plaintext tokens to disk

evals.prompt: How do I run my Python agent script and configure an MCP server so they receive my Doppler credentials without writing a .env file to disk?
evals.expected_output: Explains using doppler run -- to inject environment variables into memory at runtime and keeping MCP configs clean by launching the agent via doppler run.
expectations: Demonstrates runtime injection using doppler run -- <command>
Explains launching agent session with doppler run to inherit credentials into MCP servers
Emphasizes zero disk exposure and preventing plaintext tokens in git

evals.prompt: How do I retrieve credentials stored in my Bitwarden vault and launch an agent session without saving plaintext tokens to disk?
evals.expected_output: Explains using bw CLI or get_credential.py to unlock the vault and resolve credentials dynamically into agent process memory.
expectations: Shows unlocking Bitwarden session or querying vault via bw CLI or get_credential.py
Demonstrates running agent with injected credentials directly into memory
Maintains zero plaintext credentials on host disk

evals.prompt: How do I resolve Slack tokens from Google Cloud Secret Manager for my work AI agent environment?
evals.expected_output: Explains querying GCP Secret Manager using gcloud secrets versions access or get_credential.py with project configuration.
expectations: Uses gcloud secrets versions access or get_credential.py with GCP provider
Injects credentials into memory at runtime
